title: Minimum Index of a Valid Split
summary: An element x in an integer array nums of length n is dominant if more than half of the elements are x.
statement: An element x in an integer array nums of length n is dominant if more than half of the elements are x. Given a 0-indexed integer array nums with one dominant element, find the minimum index i to split the array into two parts such that both parts have the same dominant element. If no valid split exists, return -1.
constraints: A value is dominant in an array when it appears in more than half its positions.
Split after index i so the same value is dominant in both nonempty parts.
Return the smallest valid i, or -1.
reference_solution:
def minimum_dominant_split_index(nums):
    from collections import Counter
    dominant,total=Counter(nums).most_common(1)[0];left=0
    for index,value in enumerate(nums[:-1]):
        left+=value==dominant
        if left*2>index+1 and (total-left)*2>len(nums)-index-1:return index
    return -1

hints: Any valid common dominant must be the full array’s dominant value.
Count that candidate globally, then scan its prefix count.
At each nonfinal index test strict majority in both prefix and suffix; return the first success.
If one value dominates both disjoint parts, their counts add to a strict majority overall, proving no other candidate is needed.
